cards.label: Bermondsey — James's unit
cards.text: The shutter is half up. Archie is already inside, standing well back from the shelves, the way he always does — partly the allergy, partly James.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Right. Before he starts. You've got two veins going. Two's not a hobby. Two's a supply."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "So here's the pitch. I sell. James makes. You grow it. Everyone does one job properly instead of three badly, and we split what comes in."
James has a small brass hourglass on the workbench. He turns it over while Archie talks, and again when Archie stops. It is an ordinary hourglass. He uses it to time glue.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "You are proposing that I go into business with a man who cannot stand within two metres of his own product, and someone I taught to make a pearl."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "When you say it like that it sounds bad."

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "I have a business. It carries on whatever I decide here; my clients have no interest in who your friends are. If I put my name to a second one, I want two things first."

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "A market that pays, reliably. Three orders delivered in full. Not most of an order — in full. Whatever you have already delivered counts. I have no wish to watch you repeat yourself."

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "And a serious investment. Anyone can sell a few jars. I want to see you put money into this that you would miss."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Market and money. Done." He's already on his phone. "I'll send you proper orders — buyers I know pay. They'll come through on BizBrief."
James turns the hourglass once more and goes back to his glue. He has not said yes. He has not said no, either, and Archie is treating that as a signature.
